issues.legal_issue: A requirement to deposit disputed tax before a statutory appeal is entertained, with hardship relief limited to part of the deposit, does not violate equality or make the right of appeal illusory.
material_facts: Property owners challenged revised property-tax assessments through statutory appeals and sought interim relief from payment while those appeals were pending.
The law required the disputed tax, or the tax calculated on the disputed rateable value, to be deposited before an appeal could be entertained.
A judge could relieve an appellant from part of the deposit on grounds of undue hardship, but the relief was capped at a portion of the deposit.
The property owners challenged the deposit requirement and the cap on hardship relief as unconstitutional.
issues.conclusion: The deposit requirement, including the limit on hardship relief, is constitutionally valid and does not violate Article 14 or nullify the statutory right of appeal.
issues.legal_principle: Article 14 does not prohibit a legislature from attaching conditions to a statutory right of appeal. A pre-deposit requirement regulates the exercise of that right and balances the appellant’s right to challenge tax with the public authority’s interest in recovering it. A disadvantage resulting from an appellant’s own default does not create unconstitutional discrimination where the condition applies equally and hardship relief is available. The Court relied on Section 406(2)(e) and its proviso of the Bombay Provincial Municipal Corporations Act, 1949, and noted the complaint procedure under Section 406(2)(c) and the arbitration procedure under Section 408. It applied The Anant Mills Co. Ltd. v. State of Gujarat, Smt. Ganga Bai v. Vijay Kumar, Shyam Kishore v. Municipal Corporation of Delhi, and Vijay Prakash D. Mehta v. Collector of Customs (Preventive), Bombay.

rule.if: tax_appeal_predeposit_challenge and statutory_appeal_right and deposit_required_before_appeal and hardship_relief_available and relief_limited_to_part_of_deposit and condition_applies_equally and nonpayment_without_undue_hardship_bars_appeal

predicates.tax_appeal_predeposit_challenge: A party in a tax proceeding challenged the constitutionality of a requirement to deposit money before an appeal could be entertained.
predicates.statutory_appeal_right: The legislature created a right for an aggrieved person to appeal a tax determination.
predicates.deposit_required_before_appeal: The law required an appellant to deposit the disputed tax, or tax calculated on the disputed valuation, before the appeal could be entertained.
predicates.hardship_relief_available: A judge could reduce or dispense with the deposit when it would cause undue hardship to the appellant.
predicates.relief_limited_to_part_of_deposit: The law limited how much of the required deposit the judge could waive or dispense with.
predicates.condition_applies_equally: The deposit condition applied to all persons seeking the relevant statutory appeal.
predicates.nonpayment_without_undue_hardship_bars_a: An appellant who did not deposit the required amount and could not establish undue hardship could not have the appeal entertained.

issues.definition: When a tax appellant challenges a generally applicable pre-deposit condition attached to a statutory appeal, and hardship relief is available but limited, the condition is constitutionally valid if failure to pay without undue hardship bars the appeal.
